analysis.investment_thesis: Unified Data-Tech is a small-cap IT services play in a crowded sector, but an ROE of just 0.36% is completely disqualifying against my >15% threshold. At 21x P/E with sub-1% returns on equity, the market is pricing in a transformation that has no evidence behind it.
key_strengths: Promoter holding at a healthy 60.39% — skin in the game intact
IT services sector benefits from India's structural export tailwind
Small market cap of INR 619 Cr allows room to scale if execution improves
key_risks: ROE of 0.36% is abysmal — capital is being destroyed, not compounded
21x P/E unjustifiable for a sub-1% ROE business; no margin of safety
Tiny institutional interest (FII 0.57%, DII 5.89%) signals low conviction and poor liquidity
red_flags: ROE near zero suggests either bloated equity from recent IPO/fundraise or collapsing profitability
Revenue growth, debt levels, and operating margins not disclosed — insufficient transparency
Generic 'customized IT solutions' pitch without clear niche or moat
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Bhai, I love India's IT story — but this is not the horse to bet on. An ROE of 0.36% tells me the business is earning almost nothing on shareholder capital. Even if this is a post-IPO equity inflation artifact, paying 21x earnings for a company that cannot deploy capital productively is not value, not growth — it is hope. In IT services, the champions (TCS, Infosys, Persistent, Coforge) compound at 20-30% ROE. A sub-1% ROE in the same sector means the business lacks pricing power, scale, or execution.

Promoter holding of 60% is the one thing I like — alignment is there. But conviction needs more than alignment; it needs a business model that earns its cost of capital. With no visibility on revenue growth, margins, debt, or client concentration, and with institutional ownership barely above 6% combined, this is a speculative micro-cap, not a Jhunjhunwala-style multi-bagger. I would wait 4-6 quarters to see if ROE moves meaningfully above 15% before even revisiting. Avoid.
